Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The Pakistan players stride out to the middle, followed by Kraigg Brathwaite and Kieran Powell. Mohammad Abbas will start with the ball for Pakistan.

West Indies will have to credit Jayden Seales! He was sensational in the Test match and has put the hosts back on top. He took his first 5-fer and that is a terrific performance from the speedster. Kemar Roach was also brilliant as the experienced man bowled probing lines and lengths and was rewarded with three wickets. The target for them is 168 but this is not the best of pitches for batting and Pakistan have a very good bowling line-up. The 4th innings begins a while. Do join us then.

Pakistan have had a tough time with the bat! They lost Imran Butt early and Azhar Ali and Abid Ali strung around for a while before getting dismissed. Fawad Alam could not do much while Rizwan looked good before he was sent packing. Babar Azam was brilliant for his fifty but he needed to continue. He was well supported by Faheem Ashraf but they fell quickly on Day 4 and Pakistan lost the momentum. Hasan Ali did hit a few lusty blows towards the end but they might still be short.

What a morning for West Indies! They have taken the last 5 wickets pretty quickly and they would need 168 runs to win the first game and take a lead in the series. They will be pleased with the effort and it is the 19-year old who leads them off the field. Superb performance from the young man. Pakistan will be disappointed and now they would need to bowl really well if they want to defend this score.

OUT! CAUGHT! Jayden Seales takes a five-fer! What an excellent performance from the young man! Short ball around middle, Hasan Ali looks to pull but it takes the top edge and goes to fine leg where Kemar Roach takes a good catch. Pakistan have been bowled out for 203.
Commentary.Howout: c Kemar Roach b Jayden Seales

We are all set to begin! The West Indies' players make their way out to the middle, followed by Babar Azam and Faheem Ashraf. Kemar Roach will start with the ball.

Pitch report - Samuel Badree and Stacy Ann-King are there for the pitch report. Stacy says that on Day 3 saw some variable bounce and Chase too got some turn on this wicket. Badree says that there are some cracks developing and there is less grass on this surface.

Azhar Ali is there for a chat. He says that it is going to be a very exciting game and that is the beauty of Test cricket. Adds that they would look to build partnerships and they will have a chance of winning. Goes onto say that you are never in on this surface and if they do what is needed today, they can win. States that there is quite a lot of moisture on this pitch and in the second innings, the ball came nicely to the bat. Goes onto say seamers have dominated and they need to take responsibility on this pitch.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 4th day's play between West Indies and Pakistan. Pakistan have done well to bring themselves back in the game as they lead by 124 and still have 5 wickets in hand. Babar Azam is still out there in the middle and is looking in good touch while Faheem Ashraf has supported him well. West Indies would look to wrap up the innings as quickly as possible before the lead goes out of hand. An exciting contest awaits us on Day 4.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Right then. Pakistan will be looking to swell their lead up to something huge, whereas, West Indies will be hoping to restrict them from doing the same. The action on Day 4 will begin 30 minutes earlier, due to the time lost due to rain and the first ball will be bowled at 9.30 am local (2.30 pm GMT). Do join us then. Cheers and take care!

Jayden Seales is down for a chat. He says that he is enjoying bowling on the surface so far. Adds that something around 200 would be a good target on this wicket. Signs off by saying that they will look to pick up early wickets on Day 4.

West Indies will not be too displeased with how this day has panned out, but after taking 5 wickets, they would have wanted to take one or two more, probably the wicket of Babar Azam, which would have put them in the driving seat. Kemar Roach was on fire, as he kept things tight and also took 2 wickets. Seales, unlike Roach, went for some runs, but his over, in which he took 2 wickets, turned the tide for the hosts. Holder got the big wicket of Rizwan too, which was an important one.
Tossed up, down leg. Babar Azam pads it away and the ball deflects off his pads and races away to the boundary. The Umpire signals it as a dead ball. THAT IS STUMPS ON DAY 3!

Pakistan started off the day very nicely, as, in just 16 balls, they dismissed the hosts out, and ended the first innings of West Indies, behind by 36 runs. Their openers did not show any resistance as Imran Butt was sent packing early. Azhar Ali and Abid Ali showed some fight, but in no time, these two, along with Fawad Alam were back in the hut. It was then, that Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan came together and decided to take matters into their own hands. They raised a 56-run stand, but Holder got the better of Rizwan too, after the rain break. Azam got to his fifty and in the able company of Ashraf, they both got through Stumps on Day 3, without any more casualties.

Another great day of Test cricket is what these two sides have served us. Yes, there was a delay due to the rain, but apart from that, it has been a smooth ride on the moving day. At the end of Day 3, Pakistan will have a wider smile, as even though they lost 5 wickets, they still have Babar Azam out in the middle, and also have a lead of 124 to their name.

Update 4.25 pm local (9.25 pm GMT) - Well, we finally have some good news for you. The conditions have been gauged by the umpires and they have decided that play will resume at 4.40 pm local (9.40 pm GMT). Play can be extended until 6.30 pm local (11.30 pm GMT). Let's hope that the rain stays away now. Bad light has been an issue in the last couple of days and we will hope that it does not hamper play today.

Update 3.30 pm local (8.30 pm GMT) - We have some good news for you good folks! The rain has eased off and the covers are coming off now too. We are hearing that there will be an inspection held at 4.15 pm local (9.15 pm GMT). Let's hope that the inspection brings yields about a starting time.

Update 3.10 pm local (8.10 pm GMT) - Images from the ground show that there is a slight drizzle on at the moment. It does not look too heavy but the rain is coming down constantly as well. There are puddles formed out on the outfield too. Let's hope for some more positive news shortly. Stay tuned.

Update 2.45 pm local (7.45 pm GMT) - Well, in a normal scenario, we should have begun with the final session of play, but the rain has continued to belt down at the Sabina Park. We will keep you updated with everything that we get. Stay tuned.
.... Day 3, Session 3 ....

A session, which you would say was shared between both sides. Pakistan would be the slightly happier side, as after being in a spot of bother, they have done well, courtesy Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan. It was an over by Jayden Seales, which opened the floodgates as he removed Abid Ali and Fawad Alam in that one over, which pushed the Asians on the back foot. Then, the duo of Azam and Rizwan came together and did extremely well to steady the ship and take them to safer shores. They played sensibly early on, but when they settled in, they started playing their strokes. Pakistan are ahead by 81 runs and will look to come out and build on the same. The Men in Maroon know that they need to break this stand and will look to do that, and then, pick some more wickets quickly. Join us for the third session at around 2.40 pm local (7.40 pm GMT), if the rain has eased down, by then.

Update 2.20 pm local (7.20 pm GMT) - It was drizzling for a while here and now, it has started to get really heavy and the umpires decide that the players should walk off now. The covers are coming on as well. The umpires decide that TEA WILL BE TAKEN EARLY!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Brilliant, brilliant bowling from Seales and he gets his second wicket of the over. Perfect line, perfect length, and it is a perfect ball to get rid of Alam. He goes back for a 3-ball duck this time. On a length, around off, the ball hits the deck and straightens this time. Fawad Alam has a poke at this, but misses, as the ball takes the outside edge, and goes to the keeper, where Joshua Da Silva takes a good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Jayden Seales

OUT! TAKEN! First ball of the new spell and Seales strikes this time. Abid Ali does not last for long here and he walks back. Not what Pakistan wanted here. Jayden Seales serves a short ball, outside the off pole. The ball hits the deck and shoots up this time. Abid Ali goes back and looks to cut this one away, but gets done by the bounce. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards Jason Holder at second slip, who moves to his left and pouches this. Pakistan leads by 29 runs!
Commentary.Howout: c Jason Holder b Jayden Seales

Short ball around middle, Azam ducks under it.

For the hosts, things have not been as planned in the first session on Day 3. First, they would have wanted to swell that lead to somewhere around the 70 or 80-run mark, but they only managed to get a 36 run lead. With the ball too, they would have been mighty pleased if they could have taken one more wicket but will be happy that two Pakistani batters were sent packing. Kemar Roach has bowled well, as he took two wickets. Holder, too, has been pretty effective with the ball in hand, but he missed a catch in the slips, which by his standards, should have been snaffled. The hosts will be looking to take wickets continuously, while Pakistan will want to build on their lead. The second session will be an interesting one. It will begin at 12.40 pm local (5.40 pm GMT). Join us shortly!

A really good session of play for Pakistan. They needed to remove the 2 wickets quickly and they did that in just 16 balls in this morning session. Shaheen struck early and also twice to bundle the Windies out, with a lead of 36. The Pakistani openers again did not show any resistance as Imran Butt was sent packing very early. After that, both the Ali's - Azhar and Abid have done well to stay out there and have also raised a 50-plus run stand, to ensure that they get a lead to their name, but right at the end of the first session, Azhar Ali was sent packing. Pakistan ended the morning session leading by 20 runs.
